correctness.rationale: Two distinct complete exact-integer algorithms returned 0,0,0,240,6640,56624 ranks, spanning all 252^2 pairs. The modular method is mathematically exact over Q(zeta_10): every k<=5 cyclotomic determinant has four coordinates bounded by k!<=120, and four distinct primitive tenth roots in F_401 force a polynomial of degree <=3 to vanish coefficientwise; 401>240 lifts zero to Z. The second method evaluates actual determinants modulo Phi_10 in Z and tests all relevant sizes. The first checker verifies all orbit profiles and the iff rank-three subgroup criterion on each pair, and the subgroup-forward statement has a Vandermonde proof. No extrapolation or floating-point inference.

value.rationale: At exactly half-sampling of the ten-point Fourier matrix, the rank determines the recoverable number of five spectral coefficients. The complete 63,504-case census quantifies loss of one versus two independent Fourier directions, identifies the precise subgroup pattern behind the deepest failures, and gives every one of nine canonical row-set conditioning-independent rank profiles. This is a motivated natural complete finite invariant, not an arbitrary slice or a renaming of the binary full-spark criterion.
